Overview

  • Goal: Indentify helpful factors and unmet needs

Conclusion

  • Stress declines over time; support seekers show higher stress, likely due to greater initial burden.

  • Communication with children varies by age, cause of death, and professional involvement.

Conclusion

  • Stress declines over time; support seekers show higher stress, likely due to greater initial burden.

  • Communication with children varies by age, cause of death, and professional involvement.

  • Caregivers rely on few providers and value early support, yet face unmet needs in guidance and coordination.

Conclusion

  • Stress declines over time; support seekers show higher stress, likely due to greater initial burden.

  • Communication with children varies by age, cause of death, and professional involvement.

  • Caregivers rely on few providers and value early support, yet face unmet needs in guidance and coordination.

  • Information seeking is common; lack of coping support worsens stress, while moderate support helps most.

Discussion

  • Self reporting bias: Stress, communication strategies , and support perceptions may be influenced by memory and emotional state etc.

Discussion

  • Self reporting bias: Stress, communication strategies , and support perceptions may be influenced by memory and emotional state etc.
  • Incomplete responses: Missing data limits comparability across some axes.

Discussion

  • Self reporting bias: Stress, communication strategies , and support perceptions may be influenced by memory and emotional state etc.
  • Incomplete responses: Missing data limits comparability across some axes.
  • Heterogeneity of cases: Families differ widely in context , number of children , cause of death and available support.

Discussion

  • Self reporting bias: Stress, communication strategies , and support perceptions may be influenced by memory and emotional state etc.
  • Incomplete responses: Missing data limits comparability across some axes.
  • Heterogeneity of cases: Families differ widely in context , number of children , cause of death and available support.
  • Timing effects: Stress and support evaluations depend on when the events occured ; this cannot always be fully controlled

Implications - Structured , early guidance could significantly reduce caregivers´ burden. - Clear communication recommendations should be made more accessible. - Timely psychological support may improve coping for both caregivers and children
